display.title: Episode 410: The Storyteller, Chapter 4 (Asarah B'Teves)
display.summary_short: Memories of Chanukah, the Hakochainik march, a father and his young children say the Shema, chapter 4 of The Storyteller, and the meaning of the fast of Asarah B'Teves.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week after Chanukah 5750. Uncle Yossi recalls the joy of the Yom Tov and leads the Hakochainik march. Story time recaps how Rabbi Yehuda, the Baal Shem Tov's shamash, was sent to be a storyteller and heard of a rich merchant who pays for new stories. A father brings his three young children to Studio 604 to say the Shema, and the oldest sings one of the Twelve Pesukim. In chapter 4 of The Storyteller, the guards at the merchant's mansion welcome Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Yitzchak offers a thousand gold pieces for every new story. He locks the door and lights a candle, but Rabbi Yehuda suddenly cannot remember a single story and breaks down in tears; the merchant calmly gives him a meal and a room, leaving him wondering why Hashem made him forget. The show closes with a talk for Asarah B'Teves: there is a time to be sad, the siege of Yerushalayim by Nevuchadnetzar that led to the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash, and the promise that these fast days will become days of joy when Moshiach comes.
display.lesson: We remember sad days in order to improve ourselves; as long as we learn Torah and keep mitzvos, Hashem guards us, and He will turn the fasts into Yomim Tovim.

date.note: 'This coming Sunday, January the 7th, is Asarah B'Teves' (10 Teves 5750 = Sunday 1990-01-07); Chanukah just ended. Tuesday before = 1990-01-02, matching the weekly estimate.
